newsitem.title: GABON: Gabon cancels Sunday's parliamentary elections.
newsitem.headline: Gabon cancels Sunday's parliamentary elections.

text.p: Gabon on Saturday cancelled its delayed parliamentary elections less than 24 hours before voters in the Central African country were to go to the polls.
Elections chief Nguema Essono, in a television news announcement, cited organisation problems stemming from chaotic local elections on October 20 for the indefinite postponement.
He listed irregularities, including "the disappearance of more than one-third of names officially established on the voter list before and after the October 20 poll".
He said some 45,000 names had been entered twice on the list of Gabon's electorate of about 479,000.
The country of 1.2 million people was to elect lawmakers for its 120-seat assembly from among 1,008 candidates on Sunday.
Nguema, president of the National elections Commission (CNE), also said there was a discrepancy between the list established by his authority and computer versions.
"As a result thousands of people would have been unable to exercise their (electoral) power tomorrow," he said.

The vote was to be Gabon's second multiparty legislative election. The first was in 1990 when the oil-producing nation yielded to democratic reforms that swept away Africa's one-party or army-ruled dictatorships after the fall of Communism.
But the transition in Gabon as elsewhere in Africa has been marred by the sheer logistics of holding elections or by control of the process by ruling cliques wanting to hang on to power.
Opposition party officials appointed to the CNE told Reuters that organisational chaos leading to the cancellation of municipal elections on October 20 had not been resolved.
"Electoral lists have been prepared but they are completely untrustworty," said Florentin Moussavou, an opposition official.
He and others said names registered for a November 24 re-run of municipal voting had disappeared from computer files.
"About 5,000 names have disappeared for one Libreville district alone," said a CNE official.
"Double registrations, underage voters, vote buying, a lack of voting cards, incorrect voting lists. It's all the same as last month," said another opposition source.

Municipal election results have not been announced but the opposition Woodcutters' Party, led by Father Paul Mba Abessole, is widely believed to have won by wide margins in Libreville, home to about a third of Gabon's population.
"The results should have been out this week but the government wanted to delay them until after the legislatives," said a commentator on opposition Radio Soleil.
Municipal election results were cancelled in Libreville and Fougamou after angry voters broke open voting boxes amid widespread allegations of election fraud.

"It's incredible. In such a small country it should be possible to organise an election. We've had at least six months to correct the registration problems," said Florentin Moussavou, an opposition party official.
President Omar Bongo's Democratic Party was expected to face strong competition from the Woodcutters' Party.
Bongo has ruled the former French colony since 1968 after the death of Gabon's founding head of state, Leon Mba.

Up to 38 people were reported killed in his disputed re-election victory in 1993 during a wave of unrest. The cancelled legislative elections were part of a tiemtable of democratic and electoral reforms brokered in Paris and approved by referendum in 1995.
